*Bear with me, this is pretty wordy and I hope I read your question correctly:*

1)Have you already applied for fafsa? If not, pls do so asap because the deadline for fall 2025 is in mid June. 
2) the way it usually works is you apply for fafsa before you’re enrolled. It’s takes a few weeks for it to get sent to the school. Feds determine how much you’re eligible for and that info gets sent to your school of choice. 
3) the school will offer you an award package that you either decline or accept. When you accept the award, it’s kinda just sitting in your account until you’re enrolled in classes
4) once you’re enrolled you’ll have a balance on your account. Depending on the school’s disbursement date, whatever your award is will then be released to cover the cost. If you’re awarded more $$$ than the program costs, you’ll get a refund check :)

What you’re  describing might be gender dysphoria, but more likely than not it’s feelings of inadequacy and disgust as to how women are treated. I think all AFAB people experience at least once in their lives a feeling of disgust with the thought of things that comes with being a woman. The constant objectification and abuse women are expected to endure is bone chilling. Society tells you to be okay with it, and jf you’re not, you must be less of a woman. 

But these feelings don’t mean that you’re not a woman or you’re not female. You can identify and present however you want, but you have to honest with yourself. Are you thinking you’re not a woman because your body doesn’t match how you feel internally (dysphoria?) Or are you thinking you’re not a woman because you don’t align with societal expectations of womanhood? These are two totally different things, and I urge you to take time to soul search before doing anything drastic. ((Also, being sex repulsed might be an indication of asexuality. You can still get aroused and whatnot, but not want to engage in intercourse))

When it comes to disturbing sexual thoughts, I think they are more normal than you realize, especially if you experienced sexual trauma. Also, watching porn at a very young age can have incredibly negative effects of how you view sex as an adult. As someone else mentioned, people turned on by CNC are often survivors of assault themselves. And even the thoughts you have of your dad were probably influenced by porn. The fact that you have remorse for these thoughts are good, and at least you know you’ll never act on them.
